_readme: Judge calibration set. 30 items are REAL historical hulu_support replies (source='real_historical') paired with precedents actually retrieved by our index. 15 items are SYNTHETIC drafts I wrote deliberately at the low end (source='synthetic_bad') -- ungrounded, over-promising, dismissive, or factually wrong -- using the SAME customer message and precedents as one of the 30 real items. The synthetic items exist because real historical replies cluster in the 3-5 range and a kappa computed on a range-restricted sample is close to meaningless; the bad items force the scale to actually be used, the standard fix for range restriction in judge/rater calibration. All 'human_scores' below were assigned by a single annotator (the author of this repo) reading the rubric in config-equivalent form in eval/judge.py -- see docs/LABELING_PROTOCOL.md for the caveat that this is single-annotator, not inter-annotator, agreement.

items.customer_text: hi- Hulu currently not working for me. Can’t log in on Roku or online. What to do?
items.draft: Apologies! You likely ran into a known issue. Thanks for bearing with us!
items.note: vague 'known issue' with the specific link stripped in our data; no real diagnostic step given
